utterances.text: And how do you then explain the telegram that was sent by their commander, Tahir Zenaj, on the occasion of the fighting around the village of Lodza? And he says that: "This is part of our recent history as a battle that was won with the professionalism, wisdom, and courage of KLA members and members of foreign troops." That's what he says in a telegram that was published publicly. And here, on several occasions, I showed documents, including FBI documents, and hearings from the Congress about the presence of Al Qaeda, bin Laden's organisation, and other foreign fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is whether the chief of mission is not aware of any of this. I would like to tender this as Exhibit 7 and then as 8. "Al Qaeda Balkan links, Kosovo/Bosnia, Kosovo/Albania," it says here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. You can submit those and we will have a look at them along with the other exhibits. Just a moment. We will ask the Registrar to note them, and we will consider them in due course and we'll see whether there's any objection. Mr. Milosevic, that is your time. Now, Mr. Wladimiroff, have you any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just say the following: The Republican Political Committee of the Senate of the United States, there are also explanations there. "From Terrorists to Partners" it is called, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. You can put those documents before us and we will consider admitting them. Now, Mr. Wladimiroff, I'm afraid time is short, but you have ten minutes if you want to ask anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Wladimiroff. Mr. Milosevic, could you clarify about the number? You said this is Exhibit 7 and 8. What are 5 and 6?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already gave these exhibits to the Registrar, and the Registrar has them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Wladimiroff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Questioned by Mr. Wladimiroff:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you first a few questions about your army experience. Besides your specialist career as an army engineer, you also got other matters, I understand from your evidence, like manning -- that is, management of manpower aspects, and other logistical tasks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been specifically trained in matters of more general military nature, such as commanding combat situations?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you explain a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been through the army Staff College and have been trained there -- and have trained as an instructor there. I have been an instructor there actually instructing on command of operational troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever been specifically trained in matters of humanitarian law?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to the degree that is required by the British army, which is that one is given a mandatory lesson at periodic intervals on stuff such as the Geneva Convention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever been in a commanding position to units that were engaged but in combat situations?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been engaged with the drafting of manuals for soldiers in the field in combat situations?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have been involved in rules of engagement, discussions and formulation in Bosnia in the -- in the IFOR and then in the SFOR when I was Chief of Staff of IFOR and SFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Do you know of any manual for combat situations of the British army or any other nation within NATO?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, any --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any manuals for combat situations of the British army or any other army within NATO? Are you familiar with these kind of --

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Each nation has its doctrine which it teaches its people in, from the moment they go to Sandhurst as a cadet until the moment they leave. So, yes, each nation has its doctrine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are familiar with the British one, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Which version?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: British army doctrine has changed a bit over the period of my service, so which particular area are we talking about, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Say the ones in the year 1999?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was quite familiar with the way doctrine evolved in support -- in respect of peacekeeping operations during my army's involvement in the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred in your evidence to the Yugoslav manual for combat situation. Have you compared that manual with the recent manual of the British army?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not line by line. I only was shown the Yugoslav version of it some weeks ago, by which stage I had left the British army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. A few other questions. One of your concerns was to avoid an anti-Serb reputation, and for that reason, you did not want to be seen with KLA commanders. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was assigned to seek and maintain these contacts?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the officers who worked directly for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And who was he?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were -- well, there were a number of them, but the one -- I would say Colonel Mayer [phoen] was the one who specifically I assigned in the first instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Was he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're asked to pause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Was this colonel directly one level under you within the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked directly to me. We had a chief of liaison which was a position which was not filled at the time that he began to work with the KLA. A chief of liaison was subsequently appointed, and so an extra level of -- of oversight was inserted in the course of January, I think January or February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And who was this liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was an Irish officer called Richard Heaslip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his rank?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was initially a colonel and was promoted to brigadier in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the general verification policy towards the KLA?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To find out as much as we could about them, to establish contacts with them, so that we could pass messages to their leadership to attempt to get them to refrain from activity that would cause reaction by the FRY forces. In other words, to maintain the ceasefire that they claimed to have -- to have instituted in the course of October 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that policy comparable to the verification policy towards the VJ and MUP?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not entirely, because when we -- when the -- when the original agreements were -- were formulated in October 1998, it was the hope and expectation that there would be a similar agreement conducted with the KLA and with the Albanian side generally. Unfortunately, that -- that agreement never came to anything. That was never produced. But work was going on in that respect to try to get an agreement with them, a formal agreement, right until about mid-December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About realities, to separate that from policies, was the verification activity towards the KLA comparable to the verification activities towards the VJ and MUP?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the greatest extent possible. I think I've made it clear earlier that you can't simply go to the telephone book and look up insurgent organisations under "I". You have to go out and find them and you have to gain their willingness to cooperate with you to any degree. And they're a very suspicious organisation who don't readily communicate with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the OSCE undertake any action to verify training facilities of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Within Kosovo, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And outside of Kosovo; for example, in Albania?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no mandate in Albania. We were the Kosovo Liberation -- we were the Kosovo -- the Kosovo Verification Mission. And we certainly, at the time we started, did not expect to have more than liaison contact with -- with other missions in other countries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, that was what I'm asking. Did you try to obtain any information about such training facilities in Albania?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you got that kind of information? You received it?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not very much. It was very sketchy. It was very difficult to get.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a verification programme for Serb paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within Kosovo, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a separate programme or was that liaised with the VJ and MUP?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an attempt to -- to make the programme -- well, there was an attempt to engage the VJ and MUP in the process of verification, which they declined to take part in. When we started, we were attempting to go lay down the broad guidelines under which we would operate. Unfortunately, they didn't want to operate under guidelines or agree any with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an officer specifically designed to deal with this programme, with the paramilitary, of your office?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, whose paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an officer of your office specifically designed to deal with this verification programme for the Serb paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paramilitary? There are Serb army and there are Serb police. Who are the Serb paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my first question again. Was there a verification programme for Serb paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean Serb police units?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm asking for Serb paramilitary units. For example, Seselj's men or that kind of units.

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no programme. We were attempting to verify all units which were legitimate arms of the Yugoslav army. If there was -- if there were paramilitaries, by which I would mean people who were not official servants of the -- of the FRY, we would have attempted to find out about them, but we would certainly have not wanted to -- to -- well, no. We would have found out as much as we could about them. There was not any attempt to make a programme, because certainly, at the start, we did not think there were any Serb paramilitaries operating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any report, that you are aware of, dealing with Serb paramilitary units being active in Kosovo during the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We became concerned that there may be, yes, in the course of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss with General Loncar the presence of paramilitary units, Serb paramilitary units in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He denied it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two final questions: The Racak incident, a video clip was made by one of your assistants, was it?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this cameraman?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he employed by the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been informed by the Yugoslav investigating magistrate at the Racak incident that weapons were found at the place and that photographs were taken of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I said, in that case, could we please have access to them, and we never got it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That's all I ask, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I obviously can't re-examine the witness certainly in relation to documents in the time allowed. I know he's flying off tomorrow, I don't know what time his flight is, and I don't know if he's able to come back tomorrow morning, but if not, I've just got a couple of questions I can ask him and I'll have to deal with exhibits in his absence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- but it will have to be tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness has come back and he's been here long enough, quite honestly. Re-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember looking at this first video clip with orange vehicles on the hill? If we can give you the map, would you be able to identify where they were or not? Do you remember where we --

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While it's coming, Your Honour, it's -- I've got quite a lot to deal with about the exhibits that the accused put in. I know we get into trouble if we run beyond quarter to. If I ask this witness three questions now and he can't come back tomorrow and I have to deal with the exhibits without him, I hope that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to assist the Chamber, please, could you look at this and point out where the vehicles were travelling, which was the first part of the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can it go on the overhead projector, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 94, tab 73. From your knowledge of the area, where were the vehicles travelling on that particular road?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were inside Racak. This is the MUP vehicles with the policemen walking alongside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were going along this road, inside the village. So it would be at about that location, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The video, at that stage, taken from there, where were the orange vehicles, so far as you could judge?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orange vehicles were on the ridge line, which would be about there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So consistent with being taken from the same vantage point by the same video person at the same time or not, or can't you say?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't say because you don't know what magnification is being used on the lens.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's as far as I can go with that in the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Second question: In the gulley where you were looking, with all the bodies, first of all, was there anybody, medical or otherwise, looking at the bodies with a view to lining up the wounds on the bodies themselves with the damage to the clothing?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there was anybody who was formally medically qualified. I do believe we had one policeman who had seen gunshot wounds at close range in the course of his service, and certainly one of the -- of the people with me had seen similar -- similar-looking bodies in Northern Ireland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to rack my brains, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But both of them indicated separately to me that they felt it was impossible for those bodies to have been killed other than in the clothes they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nobody drew to your attention any inconsistency between a bullet hole and a wound?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. None whatsoever. The opposite, rather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last question in the time allowed, although we'll look at the document tomorrow, one of the exhibits that the accused wants to produce for which we do have an English version is the report of the investigating Judge, and she says -- just give me one second to find it. She says of the weapons, in the report, that she was informed by police representatives that during the search, police -- members of the MUP had found weapons and parts of military uniforms and that "they had taken everything with them." Do you have any comment on that, on either whether it was said to you, whether it was the case, could have been the case, or whether you ever heard any such suggestion that all the weapons had been taken away by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: KAROL JOHN DREWIENKIEWICZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot remember whether it was the judge, but certainly I can remember being told that there had been weapons and equipment found and, at the time and every time subsequently when this sort of conversation took place, I said, well, you must let us see this stuff. It must be produced. We can't just go on being told about this thing and being invited to believe the speaker because it had not always been the case that everyone had been entirely honest with all of the parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honour, and I've got just one very short administrative announcement that I'll have to make before tomorrow's evidence but that's, in the time, all I can ask of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you just deal with the administrative announcement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. Tomorrow's witness, of whom the accused says he has no name, was provided to him in statement form on the 7th of February with the name written on it. It's a name he knows, I have no doubt, perfectly well from the context of the statement that's been served on him, and that witness will be giving evidence in open session. That's after I've dealt with the exhibits tomorrow, which will take a little bit of time to sort out and tidy up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And Mr. Loku, who has been hanging about.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In which case it will come after Mr. Loku, Your Honour is quite right to remind me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will deal with the exhibits tomorrow, those Defence exhibits, to see if there is any objection; if not, we'll formally admit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There are objections, Your Honour, and tidying up for the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. General, thank you for coming. That concludes your evidence. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
